notes: This is the ATND1061DAN (Dante-enabled) configuration, documented via the manufacturer's product/spec page plus the official ATND1061 User Manual (docs.audio-technica.com/all/ATND1061-UM-EN-V9.pdf) for exact rear-panel port labels (Network A/B, INPUT, OUTPUT, GPI) and Euroblock pin assignments. A second SKU variant, ATND1061LK (Audio-Technica LINK-enabled), swaps the two Dante RJ45 ports for one "Network" RJ45 (IP control/app only, 100 Mbps) plus two "Audio-Technica LINK A/B" RJ45 ports (proprietary 100 Mbps link protocol for daisy-chaining/gain-sharing multiple units), and is powered by +48V DC delivered over the A-T LINK cable rather than PoE (max 5.2W vs 7W for DAN). Both variants share identical microphone/beamforming, analog I/O, and physical specs (227.5 x 227.5 x 30mm ceiling array, PoE/LINK powered, no line-voltage AC input). Dante network speed (1 Gbps) is explicitly stated in the spec sheet, used for the eth-1g grade; no HDMI/SDI/etc. ports exist on this device — it is audio-only. GPI is a control/contact-closure port, not audio, so no bandwidth grade was set per instructions.

ports.name: Network A
ports.note: Dante network port; carries PoE (IEEE 802.3af Class 0, max 7W) that powers the unit — no separate power connector exists on this model.

ports.name: Network B
ports.note: Second Dante network port (built-in 2-port switch for daisy-chain/secondary connection); not PoE-powered.

ports.name: INPUT
ports.note: Balanced analog mic/line input, 3-pin Euroblock terminal (+Hot/-Cold/Ground); MIC or LINE level switchable; 12V phantom power available.

ports.name: OUTPUT
ports.note: Balanced analog output, 3-pin Euroblock terminal (+Hot/-Cold/Ground); output level switchable +4dBu/-10dBV/-33dBV.

ports.name: GPI
ports.note: General-purpose contact-closure control input, 3-pin Euroblock (GPI1/GPI2/Ground); function assignable in Digital Microphone Manager software.
